Each of these views has its opponents, so choose; for i'rab goes back to the taste and judgement of the one parsing, provided that it does not conflict with the intended meaning of the speech.
I say: the preferred view in my opinion is the first, and its implied form is: "that prohibition — We recompensed them with it", with the preposition and its genitive noun omitted, as it is understood from the context of the speech.

safi-cedvel:106-107.t:
* I'rab:
(اتبع) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you" (أنت). (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) «[Note: Some allowed (ما) to be a maṣdar-forming particle, the interpreted maṣdar being the object of اتّبع; in that case the preposition and its genitive noun become the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).]». (أوحي) a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it" (هو), and it is the referent (ʿāʾid) — i.e. the Qur'an. (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أوحي). (من رب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أوحي) «[Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nāʾib fāʿil.]», and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (لا إله إلا هو) its i'rab has just been given «[Note: In āya (102) of this sūra.]». (الواو) conjunction. (أعرض) like اتّبع. (عن المشركين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أعرض), and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «اتبع....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أوحي ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «لا إله إلا هو»: has no grammatical position, parenthetical between the two conjoined clauses, emphasizing the obligation to follow the revelation in the matter of tawḥīd (Divine Oneness) «[Note: It may be parsed as a ḥāl of (ربّك), i.e. from your Lord, alone (in His Oneness).]».
The clause «أعرض....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اتبع.
(107) (الواو) conjunction. (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (شاء) a past verb. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (ما) negative. (أشركوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الواو) conjunction. (ما جعلنا) like ما أشركوا, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (حفيظا). (الواو) conjunction. (ما أنت عليهم بوكيل) the i'rab of its counterpart has preceded «[Note: In āya (104) of this sūra.]».
The clause «شاء الله....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause ...
The object of شاء is omitted, i.e. "Allah had willed their belief".
The clause «ما أشركوا»: has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ما جعلناك....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause شاء الله «[Note: It may be conjoined to the clause ما أشركوا, and so it too has no grammatical position.]».
The clause «ما أنت.... بوكيل»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما جعلناك.

safi-cedvel:108-108.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (لا) prohibitive, making jussive «[Translator's note: the source prints ناهبة, evidently a misprint for ناهية (prohibitive).]». (تسبوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the nūn .... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (يدعون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) .... and the wāw is the fāʿil. (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted referent (ʿāʾid) or of the relative noun itself. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya). (يسبوا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the fāʾ «[Note: The verb may be jussive, coordinated and conjoined to the verb of prohibition (لا تسبّوا).]», and the sign of the accusative is the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (عدوّا) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative «[Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because ʿadw (transgression) coincides with sabb (reviling) in meaning ... It may also be an emphatic ḥāl, i.e. "they revile Allah, transgressing".]». (بغير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an emphatic ḥāl, i.e. "being ignorant". (علم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يسبوا) is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e. "let there be no reviling of their gods on your part, lest there be reviling of Allah on theirs".
(الكاف) a preposition. (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to a mafʿūl muṭlaq whose governor is (زيّنا), i.e. "We have adorned for every community an adorning like the adorning for these" «[Note: If the kāf is a noun, it is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, because it is its description.]» ... and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address. (زيّنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... and its fāʿil «[Translator's note: the sentence is left incomplete in the source; the fāʿil is (نا).]». (لكل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (زينا). (أمة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (عمل) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (ثم) a conjunction. (إلى رب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (مرجع) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء) conjunction. (ينبئ) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "he" (هو), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الباء) a preposition. (ما) a relative noun «[Note: Or a maṣdar-forming particle, the interpreted maṣdar being in the position of the genitive ... It may also be an indefinite noun qualified by a description, the clause after it being a naʿt (adjective) of it.]», indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (ينبئهم), and the referent is omitted. (كانوا) a deficient (nāqiṣ) abrogating past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is a pronoun, the noun of kāna. (يعملون) like يدعون.
The clause «لا تسبوا....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يدعون....»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يسبوا....»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «زيّنا....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إلى ربهم مرجعهم»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to an omitted clause, i.e.:
"so they did it, then to their Lord is their return".
The clause «ينبئهم»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إلى ربهم مرجعهم.
The clause «كانوا يعملون»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما), and the referent is omitted, i.e. "they used to do it".
The clause «يعملون»: in the position of the accusative as the khabar of kāna.

* Morphology:
(عدوا): a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb عدا يعدو, of the pattern (bāb) of نصر; its wazn is فَعْل, with fatḥa then sukūn. The verb has other maṣdars: عُدُوّ with ḍamma on the ʿayn, عَداء with fatḥa on the ʿayn, عُدوان / عِدوان with ḍamma or kasra on the ʿayn, and عُدوى with ḍamma on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
1- Among the courtesies taught by the Qur'an: Allah, Glorified is He, forbade the believers from reviling the disbelievers and their gods which they associate with Allah. He gave as the reason for this that the one who is upon falsehood, if you insult what he believes in, will return the insult to you; so if you are upon the truth, you will have caused the truth to be insulted, and the religion of truth.
This Qurʾanic courtesy was, and still is, one of the social necessities, imposing itself in refined relations between nations, however much their religions differ and their creeds diverge.
And none disowns this divine guidance except the fanatics who harm religion while they reckon that they are doing good ... !

safi-cedvel:109-109.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (أقسموا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أقسموا). (جهد) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is annexed to a synonym of the maṣdar, accusative (manṣūb) «[Note: Or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "striving" or "exerting themselves" .... See āya (53) of Sūrat al-Māʾida.]». (أيمان) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (اللام) the lām that prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam). (إن) a jussive conditional particle. (جاء) a past verb, and (التاء) the tāʾ of the feminine, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (آية) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (اللام) the lām of the oath. (يؤمنن) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the retention of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of like letters ... and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil ... and the nūn is the nūn of emphasis. (الباء) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يؤمنن). (قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you" (أنت). (إنّما) a restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle. (الآيات) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (عند) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate). (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الواو) conjunction. (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the interrogative is one of disapproval (inkārī). (يشعر) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it" (هو), referring to ما. (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb — abrogating (nāsikh) — and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of anna. (إذا) an adverb of future time, stripped of the conditional sense, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, attached to (يؤمنون). (جاءت) like the first, and the fāʿil is "it" (هي). (لا) redundant (zāʾida) «[Note: It may be non-redundant; in that case (أنّها) is taken in the sense of (لعلها) "perhaps it", the clause has no grammatical position as a resumptive statement of cause, and the second object of (يشعركم) is omitted, its implied form being "their belief", i.e. "and what makes you perceive their belief? Perhaps when it comes they will not believe in it" .... And if it is non-redundant, the interpreted maṣdar is then the second object, in negated form, as if it were an answer to someone who judged them to be disbelievers forever, i.e. "and what makes you perceive their not believing in it when it comes ..."]». (يؤمنون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and the linking pronoun (rābiṭ) is omitted, i.e. "in it" (بها).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنها ... لا يؤمنون) is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of the verb يشعركم, i.e. "and what makes you perceive their belief at the time of its coming".
The clause «أقسموا....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إن جاءتهم آية ...»: has no grammatical position, an explication of the content of the oath — or parenthetical.
The clause «يؤمنن بها»: has no grammatical position, the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath.
The clause «قل ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إنما الآيات عند الله»: in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of saying).
The clause «ما يشعركم....»: in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «يشعركم....»: in the position of the nominative as the khabar of (ما).
The clause «جاءت....»: in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يؤمنون»: in the position of the nominative as the khabar of anna.

safi-cedvel:110-110.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (نقلّب) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "We" (نحن), for majesty. (أفئدة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الواو) conjunction. (أبصار) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to أفئدة, accusative, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi. (الكاف) a preposition of comparison. (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle. (لم) a particle of negation, jussive and conversion (to the past). (يؤمنوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the nūn ...
and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤمنوا). (أول) an adverb of time, accusative «[Note: i.e. at the coming down of the earlier signs in response to their demands, such as the splitting of the moon ...]», attached to (يؤمنوا). (مرة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما لم يؤمنوا) is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) ... i.e. "a turning like their disbelief before" «[Note: It may also be attached to an omitted element required by the context, i.e. "We turn their hearts and their eyes, so they do not believe, like their not believing before".]».
(الواو) conjunction. (نذر) like نقلّب, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (في طغيان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يعمهون), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يعمهون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «نقلب أفئدتهم»: has no grammatical position, resumptive «[Note: It may be conjoined to the clause يؤمنون in the previous āya, falling under the scope of وما يشعركم, i.e. "and what makes you perceive that We turn their hearts" (see al-Jamal in his gloss on al-Jalālayn).]».
The clause «لم يؤمنوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «نذرهم....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نقلب.
The clause «يعمهون»: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of (نذرهم) ..... or it is a second object if (نذرهم) is taken in the sense of one of the verbs of transformation, i.e. "We make them wander blindly in their transgression".

* Morphology:
(أفئدة): plural of فؤاد, a non-derived (jāmid) noun for the heart or the mind. From it is derived the verb فأده يفأده, of the pattern (bāb) of فتح, when one strikes his heart, and فئد يفأد, of the pattern of فرح, when one complains of his heart. Its wazn is فُعال, with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
[End of Part Seven, followed by Part Eight] Part Eight
The remainder of Sūrat al-Anʿām
From āya 111 to āya 165

safi-cedvel:111-111.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (أن) a particle resembling the verb — abrogating (nāsikh) — and (نا) a pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the noun of anna. (نزلنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil (agent). (إلى) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نزلنا). (الملائكة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أننا نزلنا....) is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being "it were established" (ثبت).
(الواو) conjunction. (كلم) a past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الموتى) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma. (الواو) conjunction. (حشرنا) like نزلنا. (عليهم) like إليهم, attached to (حشرنا). (كل) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (قبلا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the object of حشرنا. (ما) negative. (كانوا) a deficient (nāqiṣ) past verb — abrogating — indeclinable on the ḍamma:
and the wāw is a pronoun, the noun of kāna. (اللام) the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), or of disapproval. (يؤمنوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يؤمنوا) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna, i.e. "they were not fit for belief".
(إلا) a particle of exception. (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that makes accusative. (يشاء) an imperfect verb, accusative. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative, and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يشاء الله) is in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) «[Note: Or it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), i.e. "they were not to believe in any state except the state of Allah's willing".]».
(الواو) conjunction. (لكن) a particle resembling the verb — abrogating — for rectification (istidrāk). (أكثر) the noun of lākinna, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يجهلون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the retention of the nūn ... and the wāw is an attached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
The clause «(ثبت) نزول الملائكة....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «نزلنا....»: in the position of the nominative as the khabar of anna.
The clause «كلمهم الموتى»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «حشرنا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ما كانوا....»: has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يؤمنوا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يشاء الله»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second particle relative (أن).
The clause «لكن أكثرهم....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يجهلون»: in the position of the nominative as the khabar of lākinna.

* Morphology:
(قبلا): plural of قبيل in the sense of "guarantor", like رغيف and رغف, or in the sense of "group"; the first is a derived adjective, and the second is a collective noun (ism jamʿ). Its wazn is فعيل, and the plural فُعُل with two ḍammas ... There is also a view that it is the opposite of دبر (back), i.e. face to face and in plain sight.

safi-cedvel:148-148.t:
* I'rab:
(السين) a particle of the future. (يقول) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent). (أشركوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil. (لو) a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. (شاء) a past verb. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (ما) a particle of negation. (أشركنا) a past verb and its fāʿil. (الواو) a conjunction. (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to reinforce the negation. (آباء) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the agent pronoun نا, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) [Note: It is said that (لا) made unnecessary the presence of the detached pronoun before the conjunction, as the rule requires.]. (الواو) a conjunction. (لا حرّمنا) like ما أشركنا. (من) a redundant preposition. (شيء) genitive (majrūr) in form, accusative (manṣūb) in position as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الكاف) a preposition [Note: Or a noun meaning "like", in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is its qualifier.]. (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq whose governing word is the verb after it, i.e. "those before them denied with a denial like that denial which these did" ... the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. (كذّب) like شاء. (الذين) like the first. (من) a preposition. (قبل) a noun made genitive by the preposition, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition. (ذاقوا) like أشركوا. (بأس) a direct object, accusative, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن ذاقوا) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (كذّب).
(قل) an imperative verb; the fāʿil is "you". (هل) an interrogative particle of disapproval. (عند) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to a fronted khabar (predicate). (من) a redundant preposition. (علم) genitive in form, nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation. (تخرجوا) an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after the fāʾ; the sign of the subjunctive is the omission of the nūn .... the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) a pronoun, direct object. (اللام) a preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تخرجوه).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تخرجوه) is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the maṣdar implied in the preceding speech, i.e. "is there any knowledge with you, and your bringing it out to us ..."
(إن) a particle of negation. (تتبعون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... the wāw is the fāʿil. (إلّا) a particle of restriction. (الظنّ) a direct object, accusative. (الواو) a conjunction. (إن) like the first. (أنتم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ. (إلّا) like the first. (تخرصون) like تتّبعون.
The clause «سيقول الذين ... »: no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أشركوا»: no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لو شاء الله»: in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ما أشركنا»: no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لا حرّمنا ... »: no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما أشركنا.
The clause «كذّب الذين....»: no grammatical position, resumptive — or parenthetical. The clause «ذاقوا....»: no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «قل....»: no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «هل عندكم من علم»: in the position of accusative as the speech reported.
The clause «تخرجون....» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has فتخرجوه]: no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «إن تتبعون....»: no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إن أنتم إلّا تخرصون»: no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تتّبعون.
The clause «تخرصون»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).

* Morphology:
(ذاقوا): it contains an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its original form is ذوقوا: the wāw was voweled after a fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif. Its pattern is فعلوا.

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz mursal (metonymic trope): in His saying, the Exalted, «قُلْ هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ عِلْمٍ فَتُخْرِجُوهُ لَنا».
The meaning of فتخرجوه لنا is "so that you make it manifest to us"; He expressed it with "bringing out" because that is a cause of making it manifest and establishing proof for it. So its relation is causality.

* Benefits:
1- His saying, the Exalted: سَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا ... to the end of the verse.
This verse is a foreshadowing of those tendencies that appeared later among the philosophical sects in Islam: the Jabriyya, the Qadariyya, the Murjiʾa, the Muʿtazila, and other such currents, some of which may conflict with the tolerant Islamic creed, which is far from contradiction and complication.

safi-cedvel:149-149.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb; the fāʿil (agent) is "you". (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition. (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate). (الحجّة) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (البالغة) a naʿt (adjective) of الحجّة, nominative. (الفاء) a conjunction. (لو شاء): its i'rab has already been given [Note: In the previous verse.]. (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو. (هدى) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "He". (أجمعين) tawkīd (emphasis) of the second-person pronoun in (هداكم), accusative (manṣūb); the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ [Note: Emphasis with (أجمعين) is permissible without the word كلّكم preceding it, as is stated in its chapter.].
The clause «قل....»: no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لله الحجّة ... »: in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have no proof, then to Allah belongs the proof" .... and the conditional clause together with its apodosis is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لو شاء....»: in the position of accusative, conjoined to the conditional clause that is the speech reported.
The clause «هداكم ... »: no grammatical position, the apodosis of the condition لو.

* Morphology:
(البالغة): feminine of البالغ, active participle of the triliteral بلغ; its pattern is فاعلة.

* Benefits:
1- Emphasis is made with the words أجمعين, جمعاء, أجمع and جمع, either alone or after the word كلّ; these words are not put in the dual, because the words كلا and كلتا make their dual unnecessary.
Ibn Mālik says on this subject:
وبعد كلّ أكّدوا بأجمعا ... جمعاء أجمعين ثم جمعا
(And after كلّ they emphasised with أجمع, جمعاء, أجمعين and then جمع;)
ودون كل قد يجيء أجمع ... جمعا أجمعون ثم جمع
(and without كلّ there may come أجمع, جمعاء, أجمعون and then جمع.)

safi-cedvel:150-150.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) like the preceding [Note: In the previous verse.]. (هلمّ) a verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl amr) meaning "bring", and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you (plural)". (شهداء) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of شهداء. (يشهدون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... the wāw is the fāʿil. (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh). (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of anna, accusative. (حرّم) a past verb; the fāʿil is "He". (ها) a particle of alerting. (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a direct object.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله حرّم ... ) is in the position of genitive by an omitted bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يشهدون).
(الفاء) a conjunction. (إن) a conditional particle causing the jussive. (شهدوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ... the wāw is the fāʿil. (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (لا) the prohibitive lā causing the jussive. (تشهد) an imperfect verb, jussive; the fāʿil is "you". (مع) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (تشهد), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) a conjunction. (لا تتّبع) like لا تشهد. (أهواء) a direct object, accusative. (الذين) a relative, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (كذّبوا) like شهدوا, and it has no position. (بآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كذّبوا), and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) a conjunction. (الذين) a relative, conjoined to the first, in the position of genitive. (لا) a particle of negation. (يؤمنون) like يشهدون. (بالآخرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤمنون). (الواو) a conjunction. (هم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (بربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يعدلون), and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يعدلون) like يشهدون.
The clause «قل ... »: no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «سلّم شهداءكم» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has هلمّ شهداءكم]: in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يشهدون»: no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «حرّم هذا»: in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of anna.
The clause «إن شهدوا ... »: no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لا تشهد ... »: in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لا تتّبع»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «كذّبوا ... »: no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «لا يؤمنون ... »: no grammatical position, the ṣila of the third relative (الذين).
The clause «هم ... يعدلون»: no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause لا يؤمنون.
The clause «يعدلون»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(هلمّ): a verbal noun of command; it has a single form in the dialect of the Ḥijāzīs, whereas in the dialect of Tamīm the pronouns are attached to it: هلما, هلموا, and هلمّي ... The mīm has fatḥa in both dialects when the noun is assigned to the pronoun of the masculine singular (هلمّ).

* Rhetoric:
1- Putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun: in His saying, the Exalted, «وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا», to indicate that whoever denies the signs of Allah the Exalted and sets up others as equal to Him is a follower of whim and nothing else, and that whoever follows the proof can only be one who affirms it.
2- His saying, the Exalted, «فَلا تَشْهَدْ مَعَهُمْ», i.e. do not believe them, for it is sheer falsehood, and make its corruption clear to them, because conceding it to them would be agreeing with them in the false testimony, and silence may suggest approval. The intending of this meaning by «لا تشهد» is either by way of a dependent metaphor (istiʿāra tabaʿiyya) or a majāz mursal (metonymic trope) of mentioning the concomitant and intending what it entails, because testimony is among the concomitants of conceding.

* Benefits:
2- هلمّ can be intransitive or transitive, and it is one of the verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl). There are two views on its usage. The first, which is the more likely: it is not inflected, and the singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine are all the same in it. The second: it is inflected, so it is a verb and the pronouns are attached to it, so one says هلما, هلموا, هلمي, هلممن ... etc.; and the heavy nūn of emphasis may be attached to it, so one says:
هلمّن يا رجل and هلمّن يا امرأة ... etc.
[Translator's note: The source numbers this benefit "2-" with no preceding "1-".]
